To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the latewood lignin of treeline Norway spruces was positively related to the mean temperature of September–October, whereas maximum density was correlated to the mean temperature during the August–September period.

(i) the latewood lignin of treeline Norway spruces is influenced by the climatic conditions during the growing season; (ii) the latewood maximum density and the latewood lignification show a similar pattern; (iii) the latewood ring width of Norway spruce is positively correlated with the mean temperature of July and August.
the latewood lignin of treeline Norway spruces is susceptible to the effects of climate variability and, therefore, can be used as a climate proxy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of temperature on the latewood lignin in the terminal tracheids of Norway spruce.
the question of whether the climatic sensitivity of the lignification process is related to that of the maximum density and total width of annual growth rings.
the influence of temperature on the latewood lignin in treeline Norway Spruce compared with the maximum density and ring widths.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
latewood lignin formation in treeline spruce is most strongly correlated with the temperature during the period from the beginning of the autumn to mid-October.
the temperature in the growing season influences the lignification of the terminal late wood tracheids, and that the lignification of these tracheids is a good indicator for climatic variability.
the temperature during the late growing season is the most important environmental factor influencing the formation of the latewood lignin in Norway spruce.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the temperature in autumn is an important determinant of the lignin content of latewood tracheid secondary cell walls in Norway spruce, which is a factor that may be important in the context of the treeline.
treeline Norway spruces are able to respond to climatic variability, and that this is expressed in their latewood lignin contents.
the latewood lignin of treeline Norway spruces is positively correlated with the mean temperature of the period running from mid-July to the third week in October.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the latewood lignin of treeline spruce responds positively to the temperature of the period running from early September until late October.
the latewood lignin of the treeline Norway spruces is influenced by the temperature in autumn.
the latewood lignin concentration in treeline Norway Spruce is positively correlated with the mean temperature of September–October.
